{{Short description|Chemical engineer}}
'''Enrique Iglesia''' is a [[Chemical engineering|chemical engineer]] who holds the Theodore Vermeulen Chair in Chemical Engineering at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Berkeley innovators named fellows of National Academy of Inventors {{!}} Research UC Berkeley |url=https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/news/berkeley-innovators-named-fellows-national-academy-inventors |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=vcresearch.berkeley.edu}}</ref> He is a Faculty Senior Scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley]],<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=2018 Annual Meeting Honors Ceremony Recap {{!}} PressReleasePoint |url=https://www.pressreleasepoint.com/2018-annual-meeting-honors-ceremony-recap |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=www.pressreleasepoint.com |language=en}}</ref> and he previously served as the Director of the UC Berkeley Catalysis Center.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2016-12-14 |title=11 innovative UC researchers elected to National Academy of Inventors |url=https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/11-innovative-uc-researchers-elected-national-academy-inventors |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=University of California |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Iglesia was born in [[Cuba]] and his family is originally from Spain. In 1969, his family relocated to the United States. As a young immigrant with limited English, he developed an interest in mathematics and chemistry subjects because they did not rely heavily on his language skills. His strengths in these subjects were recognized by his teachers, who, despite his language barrier, encouraged him to apply to top universities.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=SAC portrait: Professor Enrique Iglesia |url=http://iglesia.cchem.berkeley.edu/iCSI_Interview_Enrique%20Iglesia_2019.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316085701/http://iglesia.cchem.berkeley.edu/iCSI_Interview_Enrique%20Iglesia_2019.pdf |archive-date=2023-03-16 |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=industrial Catalysis Science and Innovation |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Education ==
Iglesia attended [[Princeton University]] from 1973 to 1977, where he studied chemical engineering.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2020-10-05 |title=Iglesia Honored by North American Catalysis Society |url=https://www.pnnl.gov/news-media/iglesia-honored-north-american-catalysis-society |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=www.pnnl.gov |language=en}}</ref> He received his B.S degree as the top-ranked graduating senior in the College of Engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 ACS National Award Winners |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/83/i2/2005-ACS-NATIONAL-AWARD-WINNERS.html |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |date=21 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He completed an internship at Exxon's corporate research laboratories as a research associate,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Linda Wang |date=2020-01-06 |title=2020 ACS National Award winners |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/cen-09801-awards |journal=C&EN Global Enterprise |volume=98 |issue=1 |pages=36–51 |doi=10.1021/cen-09801-awards|url-access=subscription }}</ref> where he worked on engineering problems and found an interest in [[catalysis]]. Iglesia received his [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Stanford University]] in 1979.<ref name=":2" /> After he received his PhD at Stanford University in 1982.<ref name=":4" />

== Career ==
Iglesia began his professional career at [[Exxon Research and Engineering Company|Exxon Research]] where he worked on catalytic processes relevant to energy. In 1993 he joined the faculty at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he was Professor of Chemical Engineering in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering and was later appointed to the Theodore Vermeulen Chair in Chemical Engineering in 2009.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Enrique Iglesia appointed to the Royal Academy of Sciences {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/enrique-iglesia-appointed-royal-academy-sciences |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> Iglesia was recognized for his dedication to teaching and mentorship and received the Donald Sterling Noyce Teaching Prize, the highest teaching honor in the physical sciences at UC Berkeley.<ref name=":5" /> Iglesia served as Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Journal of Catalysis]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Enrique Iglesia {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/people/enrique-iglesia |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> Among one of his innovations is a [[zeolite]] based technology that is currently used as a catalyst in oil and chemical industry.<ref name=":0" /> Iglesia was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2015 for his work in chemical engineering and catalysis, especially related to sustainable energy processes and environmental protection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-06 |title=Enrique Iglesia {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/enrique-iglesia |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref> He worked as a scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley National Lab]].<ref name=":0" /> Iglesia is one of 175 top inventors named as a fellow by the [[National Academy of Inventors]].<ref name=":0" />

== Achievements and awards ==
Iglesia was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=02.12.2008 - Three faculty elected to National Academy of Engineering |url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2008/02/12_academy.shtml |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=newsarchive.berkeley.edu}}</ref> He was also elected to the [[National Academy of Inventors]] in 2016.<ref name=":0" />

Iglesia received the [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] Award for Chemical Engineering Research in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-03-28 |title=Alpha Chi Sigma Award for Chemical Engineering Research |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/awards/alpha-chi-sigma-award-chemical-engineering-research |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=www.aiche.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2012 he received the [[Gabor A. Somorjai]] Award for Creative Research in Catalysis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/gabor-somorjai-award-for-creative-research-in-catalysis/past-recipients.html |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> In 2018 he received the William H. Walker Award for Excellence in Contributions to Chemical Engineering Literature.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-03-28 |title=William H. Walker Award for Excellence in Contributions to Chemical Engineering Literature |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/awards/william-h-walker-award-excellence-contributions-chemical-engineering-literature |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=www.aiche.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2019 he received the [[Michel Boudart]] Award for the Advancement of Catalysis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Enrique Iglesia is the recipient of the 2019 Michel Boudart Award for the Advancement of Catalysis {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/enrique-iglesia-recipient-2019-michel-boudart-award-advancement-catalysis |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> He was awarded the 2021 NACS Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Catalysis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-07-03 |title=Announcement of 2021 NACS Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Catalysis {{!}} North American Catalysis Society |url=https://nacatsoc.org/news/announcement-of-2021-nacs-award-for-distinguished-service-in-the-advancement-of-catalysis/ |access-date=2025-05-17 |language=en-US}}</ref> He was also awarded the 2023 [[Faraday Lectureship Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Enrique Iglesia - 2023 Faraday open Prize: Faraday Lectureship Prize winner |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2023-winners/professor-enrique-iglesia/ |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Iglesia is a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]], [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]], [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]],<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Enrique Iglesia - Davidson School of Chemical Engineering |url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/ChE/people/ptProfile?resource_id=286482 |access-date=2025-05-17 |website=Davidson School of Chemical Engineering - Purdue University |language=en}}</ref> [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Academy of Arts and Sciences - 2015 Fellows And Their Affiliations At The Time Of Election |url=https://www.amacad.org/sites/default/files/academy/multimedia/pdfs/alphalist2015.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250502003155/https://www.amacad.org/sites/default/files/academy/multimedia/pdfs/alphalist2015.pdf |archive-date=May 2, 2025 |access-date=December 16, 2025}}</ref> and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name=":6" /> He is also an Honorary Fellow of the Chinese Chemical Society and was a [[Neil Armstrong]] Visiting Fellow of [[Purdue University]] from 2018 to 2021.<ref name=":6" />
